_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in adult patients hospitalized for an acute medical illness who are at risk for thromboembolic complications due to moderate or severe restricted mobility and other risk factors for VTE.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: APEX (Acute Medically Ill Prevention with Extended Duration Betrixaban Study), Study 11-019
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multinational study comparing extended-duration prophylactic betrixaban (35 to 42 days) to a shorter duration of enoxaparin; patients randomized 1:1 to betrixaban (160 mg loading dose then 80 mg once daily) plus enoxaparin placebo, or enoxaparin 40 mg SQ once daily for 6 to 14 days plus betrixaban placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients hospitalized for an acute medical illness (e.g., acutely decompensated heart failure, acute infection, acute respiratory failure, acute ischemic stroke) at risk for thromboembolic complications due to restricted mobility and other VTE risk factors.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of asymptomatic proximal DVT (between day 32 and day 47), symptomatic proximal or distal DVT, symptomatic nonfatal PE, or death from VTE (between day 1 and day 42).
pivotal_trials.result: The prespecified primary analysis in Cohort 1 of the PEOP failed to reach statistical significance: 132/1914 (6.9%) betrixaban vs 166/1956 (8.5%) enoxaparin, relative risk 0.806 (95% CI 0.647, 1.004), p=0.054. Exploratory overall PEOP: 165/3112 (5.3%) vs 223/3174 (7.0%), RR 0.760 (95% CI 0.625, 0.923).

nct_ctgov.title: Acute Medically Ill VTE Prevention With Extended Duration Betrixaban Study (The APEX Study)

key_safety: The most common adverse reaction (incidence >5%) was bleeding, with major bleeding in <1% of patients. Major bleeding: 25 (0.67%) betrixaban vs 21 (0.57%) enoxaparin (RR 1.19; 95% CI 0.67, 2.12). Clinically relevant non-major bleeding was higher with betrixaban: 91 (2.45%) vs 38 (1.02%) (RR 2.39; 95% CI 1.64, 3.49; p < 0.001). Most common non-bleeding adverse reactions (>=2%) included urinary tract infection (3%), constipation (3%), hypokalemia (3%), hypertension (2%), headache (2%), nausea (2%) and diarrhea (2%).
target_moa: Betrixaban is a benzamidine-based small molecule that directly inhibits the active site of factor Xa (FXa), decreasing thrombin generation in the coagulation cascade.
modality: Small molecule (benzamidine-based oral factor Xa inhibitor).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SPINAL/EPIDURAL HEMATOMA. Epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture; risk increased by in-dwelling epidural catheters or concomitant products affecting hemostasis; these hematomas may result in long-term or permanent paralysis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because betrixaban is not the first in its class and the safety evaluation did not raise issues requiring discussion.

basis.text: Priority review was granted because betrixaban is intended to prevent a serious life-threatening disease where currently no approved drug is available.

summary.text: NDA 208383 was submitted by Portola on October 24, 2016 and received priority review because betrixaban is intended to prevent a serious life-threatening disease with no approved drug available; approval was based on the single pivotal Phase 3 APEX trial. It was not referred to an advisory committee because the drug is not first in its class.

requirement.text: PMR 3229-2: Conduct a venous thromboembolism prophylaxis study in immobilized adolescents hospitalized for acute medical or surgical disease (single-arm, open-label study of betrixaban with point estimates compared to historical controls).

citations.quote: PMR 3229-2 Conduct a venous thromboembolism prophylaxis study in immobilized adolescents hospitalized for acute medical or surgical disease. The study will be a single-arm, open-label study of betrixaban with point estimates of events to be compared to historical controls. The objective of this study is to identify the safety and efficacy of betrixaban in the pediatric population.
